source_text:
Ἔχοντες οὖν τὸ παιδάριον, τῇ παρασκευῇ περὶ δείπνου ὥραν ἐξῆλθον διωγμῖται καὶ ἱππεῖς μετὰ τῶν συνήθων αὐτοῖς ὅπλων ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν τρέχοντες. καὶ ὀψὲ τῆς ὥρας συνεπελθόντες ἐκεῖνον μὲν εὗρον ἐν ὑπερῴῳ κατακείμενον: κἀκεῖθεν δὲ ἠδύνατο εἰς ἕτερον χωρίον ἀπελθεῖν, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἠβουλήθη εἰπών: Τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ γενέσθω.
ἀκούσας οὖν παρόντας αὐτούς, καταβὰς διελέχθη αὐτοῖς, θαυμαζόντων τῶν παρόντων τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ εὐσταθές, καὶ εἰ τοσαύτη σπουδὴ ἦν τοῦ συλληφθῆναι τοιοῦτον πρεσβύτην ἄνδρα. εὐθέως οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐκέλευσεν παρατεθῆναι φαγεῖν καὶ πιεῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, ὅσον ἂν βούλωνται, ἐξῃτήσατο δὲ αὐτούς, ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτῷ ὥραν πρὸς τὸ προσεύξασθαι ἀδεῶς.
τῶν δὲ ἐπιτρεψάντων, σταθεὶς προσηύξατο πλήρης ὢν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ οὕτως ὥστε ἐπὶ δύο ὥρας μὴ δύνασθαι σιγῆσαι καὶ ἐκπλήττεσθαι τοὺς ἀκούοντας, πολλούς τε μετανοεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ἐληλυθέναι ἐπὶ τοιοῦτον θεοπρεπῆ πρεσβύτην.
orientation: The police captain Herod and his men have just arrested a boy who confessed under torture, and now they come with him to seize Polycarp.
pass_a_gloss: Having therefore the boy, on the Preparation day about the dinner hour there went out pursuers and horsemen with their usual weapons, as if running against a robber. And late in the hour, having come upon him together, they found him lying down in an upper room; and from there he was able to go away to another place, but he was not willing, having said: The will of God let it be done. Having heard therefore that they were present, having come down he conversed with them, while those present were marveling at his age and his steadfastness, and whether there was so great eagerness for such an old man to be arrested. Immediately therefore he ordered them to have food and drink set before them at that hour, as much as they might wish, and he asked them that they give him an hour to pray without fear. And when they permitted it, having stood he prayed, being full of the grace of God, so that for two hours he was not able to be silent and those listening were astonished, and many repented that they had come against such a godly old man.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'police captain' for εἰρήναρχος; διωγμῖται are the subordinate pursuers or constables under Herod, so 'police officers' keeps the same official register.
Παρασκευή is the standard term for Friday, the day of preparation before the Sabbath; keeping 'Preparation day' preserves the Jewish calendar context of the great Sabbath that follows.

choices.english: as if running against a robber
choices.why: The simile is vivid and deliberate: they come armed as though Polycarp were a violent criminal. 'Running against' keeps the hostile motion of ἐπί with the accusative.

choices.english: The will of God let it be done
choices.why: This is a third-person imperative of γίνομαι, echoing the Lord's Prayer. The word order 'let it be done' preserves the imperative force and the passive sense.
rejected: May the will of God happen

choices.why: The noun εὐσταθές denotes calm composure and firmness under pressure, which is exactly what the onlookers marvel at in the old man. 'Steadfastness' captures both the calm and the firmness.
Θεοπρεπής means 'befitting God' or 'godly'; applied to Polycarp it marks him as one whose character reflects God. 'Godly old man' is plain and keeps the adjective-noun order.

bible_refs.note: Τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ γενέσθω closely echoes the Lord's Prayer petition γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.

pass_b_english: So they took the boy, and on the Preparation day, around the dinner hour, the pursuers and cavalry went out with their usual weapons, running as if they were chasing a robber. Late in the hour they closed in on him and found him lying down in an upper room. He could have gone from there to another place, but he refused. He said, “The will of God be done.”

When he heard that they had arrived, he came down and talked with them. Those present marveled at his age and his calm steadfastness, and at the fact that there was such eagerness to arrest so old a man. At once he ordered food and drink to be set before them at that hour, as much as they wanted, and he asked them to give him an hour to pray without fear.

They granted it, and he stood and prayed, so full of the grace of God that for two hours he could not be silent. Those who heard him were astonished, and many regretted that they had come against such a godly old man.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'police captain' for εἰρήναρχος, but 'police officers' is not fixed; more critically, 'cavalry' for ἱππεῖς is fine, but the main issue is διωγμῖται (pursuers/persecutors) rendered as 'police officers' which imposes a modern institutional term not in glossary and obscures that these are persecutors.

problems.quote: The will of God let it be done
problems.why: Greek is 'let the will of God be done,' not 'let it be done' as if 'it' refers forward; this inverts the sense to Polycarp's will rather than God's.
problems.fix: The will of God be done
problems.ruling: Greek says 'let God's will be done'; English 'let it be done' obscures the subject, risking misreading as Polycarp's will.

edits.old: the police officers and cavalry went out
edits.new: the pursuers and cavalry went out

edits.old: “The will of God let it be done.”

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'police captain' for εἰρήναρχος; 'pursuers' obscures official role.
last_rejected.ruling: διωγμῖται means pursuers; εἰρήναρχος not in source text, glossary claim irrelevant to this passage.

last_rejected.why: ὀψὲ means 'late' generally, not 'late in the hour'; context suggests late in the day.
last_rejected.ruling: ὀψὲ τῆς ὥρας 'late in the hour' is acceptable; ὀψὲ with genitive is normal, no meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified who was speaking and acting, smoothed sentence order, explained the Preparation day as Friday before the Sabbath, and made the narrative flow naturally for reading aloud while preserving every detail.

notes.quote: on the Preparation day around the dinner hour
notes.why: 'Preparation day' (parasceve) is a Jewish/Christian term for Friday before Sabbath; unexplained.
notes.fix: Add brief note: 'Preparation day' means Friday, the day before the Sabbath.
